subject: Approval request: exceptional Hosted API discount for KeyLight.ai
messages:
From: Tom Baker <tom@keylight.ai>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Jill Park <jill.legal@keylight.ai>, KeyLight Procurement <procurement@keylight.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted API pricing — request for an enterprise concession

Diego,

Thanks again for the demo earlier. We're excited about Redwood's latency and the prefix caching notes — would be a great fit for our real-time summarization product. We ran the expected token volumes through our finance model and the numbers are tight on our side.

Quick ask: the published Hosted API rates are above our acceptable unit economics for the pilot. KeyLight is prepared to commit to a 36-month contract with a minimum committed spend of $1.2M/year (billed monthly) if we can secure a below-list unit price. Specifically we're asking for a 30% discount off list Hosted API usage for the committed tier, plus an option to increase committed capacity after 12 months at the same rate.

Attachments: KeyLight_pricing_request_20261125.pdf (pdf)

Can you share what flexibility is available and the escalation path for deals requesting >20%?

Best,
Tom
Founder, KeyLight.ai
From: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Tom Baker <tom@keylight.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — request for an enterprise concession

Tom — thanks for the clear ask and for putting numbers against the commitment. I looped in our deal desk and a couple of execs to get visibility on the concession path; see internal note below.

Short answer: >20% requires executive approval and needs a clear list of compensating factors (multi-year commit, revenue protection, references, go-to-market commitment, and legal/PO cadence). Please send the mutual action plan and the procurement timeline so we can fast-track.

I attached the pricing worksheet we typically use; could you populate the expected monthly token ramp and the PO cadence? That will help the finance model.

Attachment: pricing_proposal_keylight_v3.xlsx (xlsx)

— Diego
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
From: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Escalation: Exec approval required — KeyLight request for 30% off Hosted API list

Team —

Summary: KeyLight (startup; Series B; data-sensitive SMB healthcare integrations) is requesting a 30% discount on Hosted API usage in exchange for a 36-month committed spend (~$3.6M total, $1.2M/year). They want the committed unit price fixed for the first 24 months with an option to expand. They plan to be a reference in our healthcare vertical and have procurement timelines that require a signed MSA before Jan 15 to hit their product launch.

Why this matters: 1) Material ARR if we lock it (>$1M/yr). 2) Strategic vertical reference (healthcare-focused partner). 3) They viewed Dedicated but cannot meet on-prem latency constraints; Hosted API is the path to close quickly.

Risks: 1) 30% below list materially compresses unit economics on token-heavy workloads without strict token caps/guardrails. 2) Long-term price lock without consumption protections. 3) Legal wants an explicit overage and audit clause.

Request: Executive approval to offer up to a 30% concession off list Hosted API pricing subject to the following compensating controls:
- Minimum committed spend: $1.2M/year for 36 months (non-cancellable first 12 months)
- Monthly committed token tiers with true-ups and an overage rate at list (or list - 10%)
- Quarterly business review (QBR) and a documented launch milestone schedule in the mutual action plan
- Approval contingent on Legal signoff on audit/overage clauses and SOC 2 evidence receipt

Attachments: KeyLight_MutualActionPlan_v2.docx

Requested approver: Marissa (Revenue Ops) and Sean (Head of Sales Strategy) — quick yes/no by COB Monday would keep the January timeline intact.

Thanks,
Diego
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Escalation: Exec approval required — KeyLight request for 30% off Hosted API list

Diego —

I approve the concession up to 30% under the controls you've outlined with two additional conditions: 1) include a 12-month minimum cash commitment clause (non-refundable credit against usage) and 2) implement an annual CPI+ floor on any extension pricing so we don't get locked to sub-inflation rates. Legal to own final MSA/overage language.

Sean — please confirm you have capacity to own the reference / launch enablement once signed. Lauren — looping you to ensure deal desk captures the true-up cadence and that the HubSpot deal records the committed tiers.

Marissa Cole
VP, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
